### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6c6cfcc1e271f593fe4a7919f12f855cc41e5bd5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8a2f0507eeb5be3fd6c7c99b32e0a071278b09f0` — the merge of head `30b6c84f2b0b9dff4da87be4be5c9f60b325514e` into base `6c6cfcc1e271f593fe4a7919f12f855cc41e5bd5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8a2f0507eeb5be3fd6c7c99b32e0a071278b09f0 && git checkout 8a2f0507eeb5be3fd6c7c99b32e0a071278b09f0
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6c6cfcc1e271f593fe4a7919f12f855cc41e5bd5 30b6c84f2b0b9dff4da87be4be5c9f60b325514e && git checkout -B drift-repro 6c6cfcc1e271f593fe4a7919f12f855cc41e5bd5 && git merge --no-ff 30b6c84f2b0b9dff4da87be4be5c9f60b325514e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6c6cfcc1e271f593fe4a7919f12f855cc41e5bd5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

Head-sha: `30b6c84f2b0b9dff4da87be4be5c9f60b325514e`

Scope: docs/adr/0048-cross-package-metadata-collision.md + packages/objectql/src/bare-name-one-holder.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry.ts, packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts, packages/objectql/src/registry-bare-name-one-holder-ai-family.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/bare-name-one-holder-ai-family.dogfood.test.ts, scripts/adr-anchors/packages__objectql__src__bare-name-one-holder.ts.json, .changeset/31414-bare-name-tool.md

Inputs: card #31414 (body + 6 comments, through 6726705019), PR #31661 (body, 8-file list, net diff vs merge-base `c5361e2c`), check-runs on the head (53), and the tree at `origin/claude/project-thread-7w4hop` read with `git show` only. Faces: `rules` (ADR-0048 is Tier H) and `narrowing` (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`); on the narrowing face every non-prose path of the diff was read.

Check-runs on the head: 52 of 53 completed; every completed gate-carrying run is `success` (`Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Check Changeset` ×2, `Test Core` 2/8–8/8, `Live E2E UI`, `Test UI`). **`Test Core (1/8)` is still `in_progress`** at review time, so the required `Test Core` set is not yet green; no run is red. The dogfood shards are `skipped` on the PR run (the queue leg carries them), so the booted pin in this diff has run only on the dev's side (reported 440 files / 3645 tests green at `cbd8c5b2`, same test sources as the head).

### ① Derived judgments

Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, read from the tree and judged:

1. **Package door (`SchemaRegistry.installPackage` → `refuseBareNameConflicts`, registry.ts ~8719/4736).** After the seal, a package whose manifest (or a nested `plugins[]` entry) carries `tools[].name` equal to a name another installed package holds is refused `422 NAMESPACE_CONFLICT` ahead of every mutation. Mechanism: `declaredBareNames` iterates `BARE_NAME_REGISTRY_TYPES` (derived from the list, so it now includes `tool`) over `COLLECTION_KEY.tool = 'tools'`, the same key the engine's `METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS` loop reads (`'agents', 'tools', 'skills'`, engine-top-level.ts ~4087) and `pluralToSingular('tools') === 'tool'` (spec `manifest-collection-spelling.ts:91`). The door and the seam therefore see the same items under the same type. **Right.**
2. **Item seam (`SchemaRegistry.registerItem`, registry.ts ~7673).** The guard is `packageId && isBareNameRegistryType(type) && holdsBareName(type, item) && !isOverridableBaseline(type, packageId)`; `isBareNameRegistryType('tool')` is now true, `holdsBareName` is `true` for every non-action type, `OVERRIDABLE_BASELINE_PACKAGES.tool` is empty. So a package-bound `registerItem('tool', …, 'name', pkg)` after the seal over another package's name is refused before stamping or storing. A registration with no `packageId` (the environment slot, which is exactly how cloud's Studio mirror writes `register('tool', …)`) is never judged. **Right.**
3. **Cold boot (`sealBareNameHolders`, registry.ts ~4838; sealed by `ObjectQLPlugin` at `kernel:bootstrapped`, plugin.ts 1263–1274).** The seal iterates `BARE_NAME_ONE_HOLDER_TYPES`, so a deployment already holding two `tool`s under one name warns once (`BARE_NAME_COLD_BOOT_MODE = 'warn'` unchanged) naming both holders and the rename; which holder `/meta/tool/NAME` serves is unchanged (the dogfood pin asserts `alpha`). **Right.**
4. **Hook-binder function door.** Untouched; `tool` is a registry type, not a `function`. **Right (no change).**
5. **Public surface.** `bare-name-one-holder.ts` is not exported from `packages/objectql/src/index.ts` (grep: no hit), so the `'tool'` member added to `BareNameRegistryType` and to the three `Record<…>` tables is internal vocabulary, not a public type widening. The public change is behavioural only: `BareNameConflictError` (already public via registry.ts) can now carry `type: 'tool'`, and `install-local` can now answer `422 PLUGIN_REGISTER_FAILED` for a tool. **Right — a pure narrowing of the accept set; nothing widened.**
6. **Stored data.** No stored body changes shape; no conversion; nothing rewrites stored references. **Right** (matches the changeset's `adr-0087: not-required`).
7. **Other producers of package-bound `tool` items.** Searched the tree for any `registerItem('tool'` / `register('tool'` outside the collection loop (ADR-0109's materialised `action_<name>` tools in particular): none exists in this repo; `packages/mcp` reads no metadata `tool` item (it bridges the AI service's code `ToolRegistry`). So the only package-bound producer the doors now judge is the manifest collection loop, in both its seams (manifest and nested plugin). **Right — no unintended refusal path.**
8. **Shipped producers.** On the head no example app and no platform package declares `tools:` (hits: `examples/app-showcase/scripts/mcp-fixture.mjs`, an MCP fixture script, and the CLI generator's empty `tools: []`), so no existing deployment of this repo's packages gains a boot warning. **Right** (matches the changeset's "Measured producers"; HotCRM and marketplace packages correctly marked NOT MEASURED).

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/31414-bare-name-tool.md`: `'@objectstack/objectql': minor`, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` both line-initial, exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`<!-- adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription) … -->`), and the migration ("The one-line fix: rename the tool in one of the two packages — the refusal names the namespace-prefixed name — or uninstall one of them"). The PR body carries the same two declaration lines, line-initial.
- Against AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: the kind is `narrowed` ("a value refused or a requirement tightened"), and "a kind takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves" → `minor` is the floor and is what is declared. `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and the banner is present; `no (narrowing)` is a well-formed form of the closed pair. **Level matches what the diff publishes.**
- `Clause-②` criterion (does the card widen the accept set or the public surface?): ① items 1–5 show nothing widened — the only type-level growth is an unexported union — so the answer is **`no`, arm `(narrowing)`, BREAKING. Right**, and consistent with #31375's precedent for `agent`/`skill`. The dev's first spelling `yes (narrowing)` (from claim 6725057016) was corrected by the seat's re-stated claim 6726705019 and the head carries the corrected line in both places.
- `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` — a package author's `tools[].name` is now refused under a held name after the seal: a requirement tightened. **Right.**
- `check:adr-0087-registration` and `Check Changeset` are green on the head; the marker category reads as the gate's `not-required` arm with the written reason.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev report 6726685498 (`open_questions`, `deviations`, `out_of_scope_findings`), against the seat's rulings in 6726705019:

1. **Q1 `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` → keep or restate?** Ruled **B** (restate `no (narrowing)`). The head's PR body and changeset both read `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. **Answered and implemented.**
2. **Q2 fold `tool` into the header Addenda line, §3.4's 2026-11-06 note, P1.5 and P1.9?** Ruled **B**, with ⛔ never the Status line. The diff folds `tool` into exactly those four spots and adds P1.10; the Status line (ADR line 3) is **byte-identical** to `origin/main` (diffed the first four lines: identical), so draft PR #31586's edit is not pre-empted. **Answered and implemented.** (The Addenda line is line 7, four lines below the Status line: no textual overlap with #31586; a later rebase of whichever lands second stays mechanical.)
3. **Q3 update `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__objectql__src__bare-name-one-holder.ts.json`?** Ruled **B**. The invariant gains one clause naming `tool` after the AI family; `check-adr-anchors` runs inside the green `Lint & Repo Gates`. **Answered and implemented.**
4. **Deviation: dogfood file outside `packages/objectql/src/`.** The seat's re-stated claim widened the file surface to name the booted pin. **Covered.**
5. **Deviation: verification spans two heads (`57fd18f8` / `cbd8c5b2` / `30b6c84f`).** The check-runs on `30b6c84f` are the verdicts here; see the in-progress `Test Core (1/8)` above. **Answered by the head's check-runs, one still running.**
6. **Deviation: first ablation marker restored before any run.** No trace in the diff (net diff has no marker, no stray file). **Closed.**
7. **Deviation: PR assignee/reviewer unset.** Per the standing order; the PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay on behalf of `os-steve`, as the body's attribution comment says). **No note needed.**
8. **Out-of-scope 1: cloud `ToolRegistry.register` is a `Map.set` (last wins).** Named producer, carrier cloud; the cloud seat (6725094995) offered to file it. **Escalated to the seat: confirm the cloud card exists** — the dev's report records the offer, not a filed card. Not a finding on this diff.
9. **Out-of-scope 2: cloud's Studio mirror registering package-bound after the seal — NOT MEASURED.** Recorded in the PR's Acceptance notes; by the cloud reading the mirror writes through `register('tool', …)` with no package, which ① item 2 shows is never judged, and only "when absent". **Acceptable as noted** (Prime Directive #10: noted, not buried).

### ④ Design judgment

**The ADR against its first consumer.**

- **P1.10 ↔ `bare-name-one-holder.ts`.** "`tool` joins P1.2's list, last: the same two doors, the same holders, the same envelope and rename. It is not bundled, and it has no overridable baseline and no built-in name" — the list ends `'tool'`; `BUILT_IN_BARE_NAMES.tool` and `OVERRIDABLE_BASELINE_PACKAGES.tool` are empty sets; the key is the plain `pkg:name` (no `@member` bundle). Sentence by sentence, the code agrees. The module doc's new `tool` bullet and `CONSUMER_CLAUSE.tool` ("a skill's `tools` and an MCP client name a tool") state the same measurement the note does.
- **P1.10 ↔ the two doors and the seal.** Both doors are generic over the list (① items 1–3); the plugin seals at `kernel:bootstrapped` after `kernel:ready`'s install-local rehydrate, as P1.3 says. The unit matrix (`describe.each(['agent','skill','tool'])`) pins for `tool`: package-door refusal with envelope/holders/rename and no record left, the ABLATION (pre-seal coexistence, post-seal refusal at both doors), the item seam, the nested plugin under its parent, same-package re-registration, uninstall releasing the name, the environment-slot CONTROL, the cold-boot warn, reload + third package, and `'refuse'` mode. The booted pin drives the real `install-local` door (`MarketplaceInstallLocalPlugin`) and the real cold boot (two `AppPlugin`s) and asserts `/meta/tool/NAME` keeps serving `alpha`. The three CONTROLs that replaced the old "tools coexist" CONTROL (different tool names; tool vs another package's skill/agent; one package's skill and tool under one name) are the right ones for "an agent, a skill and a tool are three types".
- **§3.4's 2026-11-06 note, P1.5, P1.9, header Addenda.** Each now names `tool` with the date and points at P1.10; §3.4's "keeps §3.4 as written" list drops `tool` and keeps the object-bound action; P1.9's "Not in the list" is correctly re-scoped to "not covered by this change" with a forward pointer; P1.5 keeps "P1.9's change closes phase 1" and adds that `tool` joined afterwards on its own card. The ADR reads whole.
- **Execution plan and red lines.** #30803 phase 1's list stays as ruled (P1.5 still says `tool` was never in the ruling's list); `tool` joins by the maintainer's acceptance of #31414, quoted in P1.10. Nothing here builds package-scoped resolution (the doors refuse; no reader gains package context), and the refusal is the phase-1 kind the epic's red line keeps in force until a type's own retirement child — consistent with the PR's "needs nothing from child R". The cold boot stays `'warn'`, as P1.3 records the 2026-11-06 ruling.
- **Measurement.** The card's rule was "if the by-name read has no package context, `tool` joins". `/meta/tool/NAME` alone satisfies it (P1.9 measured; the dogfood pin re-pins it on the head). The additional readers P1.10 cites were verified in the tree: `SkillSchema.tools` regex `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*\*?$` (skill.zod.ts:374), `registerToolFromDefinition` → `server.registerTool(tool.name, …)` / `toolName: tool.name` (mcp-server-runtime.ts 1262–1290), and `AIToolDefinition`/`ToolCallPart` carry a name only. Cloud's reading (6725094995) is quoted at its ref `ba6f0fa`.

**Attempts to break it.** (a) A second package-bound producer of `tool` items that the doors would now refuse unexpectedly: none exists (① item 7). (b) Divergence between what the door reads (`COLLECTION_KEY.tool`) and what the seam registers (`METADATA_ARRAY_KEYS` → `pluralToSingular`): both resolve `tools` → `tool`. (c) Cloud's mirror becoming a refused registration: it writes the environment slot, never judged. (d) An existing shipped clash turning a boot red: none declared; and the mode is `'warn'`. (e) Status-line collision with #31586: byte-identical to main. None breaks.

**Findings, graded:**

- **nit** — `registry.ts` ~8710, the `installPackage` door's comment still enumerates "a picklist, a mapping, a dataset, an API, an object-less action, a flow, a webhook, a connector, an email template" with no `agent`, `skill` or `tool` (the item-seam comment at ~7660 was updated; this one was not, and #31375 left it the same way). Comment only; the code is generic over the list.
- **nit** — The 2026-11-06 addendum's own status paragraph still reads "one family per change (P1.2, P1.7, P1.8, P1.9 — the last)" and does not mention P1.10; the header Addenda line, P1.5 and P1.9 do point at it, and the PR's acceptance note explains the choice (P1.10 is a dated note, not a fifth family; the ruling named four spots). No effect on the contract.
- **nit** — P1.10's sentence "the MCP bridge registers each tool under its name and calls it by that name" is true of the reference protocol but could be read as the bridge reading metadata `tool` items; in this repo `bridgeTools` reads the AI service's code `ToolRegistry`, and the note's own cloud paragraph makes the mirror/handler distinction. Wording precision only.
- **escalation (not a finding on this diff)** — the cloud `ToolRegistry` last-wins producer (③ item 8): the seat confirms a cloud card is filed.

No must-fix. No should-fix.

> `↳ 失败原因` 是判读的关键：**超时**（`Test timed out in …` / `Hook timed out in …`）多半是负载/时序，不是本 PR 的回归；
> **断言**（`AssertionError: …`）才指向真实的行为改变。两者的 `FAIL` 行长得一模一样，只有这一行能区分。
>
> ⚠️ **断言这一侧有一类例外，判据是断言在测什么，不是它是不是 `AssertionError`。** 断言的对象是**产品行为**（一个值、一个形状、一次拒收）⇒ 照上面读：真实的行为改变，去查，⛔ 不要重排掉；
> 断言的对象是**这次实验自身的有效性前提**（跑完的耗时、负载下的先后、任何只在时间预算内才成立的条件）⇒ 它跟**超时**是同一类，同样对负载敏感，重排一次是合法的判别手段。
> 识别是机械的：断言的消息或它比较的值本身点名了一段**时长、一个时间戳、一个耗时计数**。实测过的一对 —— `AssertionError: SecurityPlugin.init() ran: expected false to be true` 测的是产品行为（真回归）；
> `AssertionError: this run took over a second, so second-precision stamps could have differed too: expected 1006 to be less than 1000` 测的是实验前提：它守护的那条不变式当时是绿的，同一个 head 原样重排一次即成功。
> 穿着 `AssertionError` 外衣的时间测量，仍然是时间测量。（⛔ 这只改「怎么读一次红」，不改「哪些测试可以重排」——后者由别处管。）
